title: Coat of Anticubism
statementMd:
![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/96981139a081f7584b4197a696fccf376490b622.gif)

As some of you know, cubism is a trend in art, where the problem of constructing volumetrical shape on a plane with a combination of three-dimensional geometric shapes comes to the fore.

A famous sculptor Cicasso, whose self-portrait you can contemplate, hates cubism. He is more impressed by the idea to transmit two-dimensional objects through three-dimensional objects by using his magnificent sculptures. And his new project is connected with this. Cicasso wants to make a coat for the haters of anticubism. To do this, he wants to create a sculpture depicting a well-known geometric primitive — *convex polygon*.

Cicasso prepared for this a few blanks, which are rods with integer lengths, and now he wants to bring them together. The $*i*$-th rod is a segment of length $*l*_{*i*}$.

The sculptor plans to make a convex polygon with a nonzero area, using *all* rods he has as its sides. Each rod should be used as a side to its full length. It is forbidden to cut, break or bend rods. However, two sides may form a straight angle ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c1ad0f0cc748540b62d51359bade6ed6ac0ed12e.png).

Cicasso knows that it is impossible to make a convex polygon with a nonzero area out of the rods with the lengths which he had chosen. Cicasso does not want to leave the unused rods, so the sculptor decides to make another rod-blank with an integer length so that his problem is solvable. Of course, he wants to make it as short as possible, because the materials are expensive, and it is improper deed to spend money for nothing.

Help sculptor!

## Input

The first line contains an integer $*n*$ ($3 ≤ *n* ≤ 10^{5}$) — a number of rod-blanks.

The second line contains $*n*$ integers $*l*_{*i*}$ ($1 ≤ *l*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{9}$) — lengths of rods, which Cicasso already has. It is guaranteed that it is impossible to make a polygon with $*n*$ vertices and nonzero area using the rods Cicasso already has.

## Output

Print the only integer $*z*$ — the minimum length of the rod, so that after adding it it can be possible to construct convex polygon with $(*n* + 1)$ vertices and nonzero area from all of the rods.

## Note

In the first example triangle with sides ${1 + 1 = 2, 2, 1}$ can be formed from a set of lengths ${1, 1, 1, 2}$.

In the second example you can make a triangle with lengths ${20, 11, 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 10}$.
statementZhMd:
![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/96981139a081f7584b4197a696fccf376490b622.gif)

众所周知，立体主义是一种艺术潮流，其核心思想是：通过组合三维几何图形，在平面上构造立体形状。

著名雕塑家 Cicasso（你可以欣赏他的自画像）憎恨立体主义。他更为推崇这样一种理念：使用他宏伟的雕塑，将二维物体表现为三维物体。而他的新项目正与此有关。Cicasso 想为反立体主义的爱好者制作一件外套。为此，他想创作一件描绘著名几何图形——*凸多边形*的雕塑。

Cicasso 为此准备了一些杆件，它们的长度均为整数，现在他想将它们组合起来。第 $*i*$ 根杆件是一条长度为 $*l*_{*i*}$ 的线段。

雕塑家计划使用他拥有的**所有**杆件作为边，制作一个面积非零的凸多边形。每根杆件都必须完整地作为一条边使用。禁止切割、折断或弯曲杆件。不过，允许两条边形成平角![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c1ad0f0cc748540b62d51359bade6ed6ac0ed12e.png)。

Cicasso 知道，无法仅使用他所选的这些长度的杆件制作一个面积非零的凸多边形。Cicasso 不想留下未使用的杆件，因此决定再制作一根长度为整数的杆件，使问题变得可解。当然，他希望这根杆件尽可能短，因为材料很昂贵，毫无意义地花钱是不恰当的行为。

请帮助这位雕塑家！

## 输入格式

第一行包含一个整数 $*n*$（$3 ≤ *n* ≤ 10^{5}$）——杆件毛坯的数量。

第二行包含 $*n*$ 个整数 $*l*_{*i*}$（$1 ≤ *l*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{9}$）——Cicasso 已经拥有的杆件长度。保证无法使用这些杆件制作一个具有 $*n*$ 个顶点且面积非零的多边形。

## 输出格式

输出唯一一个整数 $*z*$——添加该长度的杆件后，能够使用所有杆件构造一个具有 $(*n* + 1)$ 个顶点且面积非零的凸多边形时，杆件的最小长度。

## 说明

在第一个样例中，可以使用长度集合 ${1, 1, 1, 2}$ 构造一个边长为 ${1 + 1 = 2, 2, 1}$ 的三角形。

在第二个样例中，可以构造一个边长为 ${20, 11, 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 10}$ 的三角形。
